buildings.name: Comitium (archaic and early Republican)
buildings.summary: The consecrated assembly ground in front of the Curia Hostilia, oriented to the cardinal points like an augural templum. Boni found more than twenty superimposed floors here from the 7th century BC onward; the Twelve Tables were displayed on bronze at its edge.

buildings.summary: Caesar moved the Rostra to the west end of the square on the main axis of the Forum, facing the Temple of Divus Julius; Antony and Octavian completed it. A curved stair at the back, a front 24 m long hung with bronze prows, and the honorific statues and columns crowded on top.

buildings.name: Atrium Libertatis (Republican, debated site)
buildings.summary: Office of the censors with their archives and the bronze tablets of the census, rebuilt in 194 BC. Asinius Pollio rebuilt it in 39 BC with Rome's first public library, perhaps elsewhere.

buildings.name: Basilica Julia (Caesarian)
buildings.summary: Caesar replaced the Basilica Sempronia with a far larger hall, dedicated unfinished in 46 BC; Augustus completed it. Burned within a few decades.

buildings.name: Basilica Julia (Augustan rebuilding)
buildings.summary: Rebuilt after the fire on a larger scale and rededicated in AD 12 in the names of Gaius and Lucius Caesar: a central hall 82 x 18 m lit by a clerestory, surrounded by two aisles and two storeys of marble-faced arcades on piers. The centumviral court sat here in four sections; gaming boards are scratched into its steps.

buildings.name: Basilica Fulvia
buildings.summary: Built by the censors M. Fulvius Nobilior and M. Aemilius Lepidus in 179 BC behind the Tabernae Argentariae; the Aemilii maintained it, decorated it with ancestral shields in 78 BC and gave it their name.

buildings.name: Basilica Paulli (Republican)
buildings.summary: L. Aemilius Paullus, consul in 50 BC and paid by Caesar, rebuilt the hall from 55 BC; his son dedicated it in 34 BC. A nave 12 m wide with two aisles on the north and one on the south, columns of africano and cipollino, and a frieze of early Roman history.

buildings.name: Basilica Paulli (Augustan)
buildings.summary: After the fire of 14 BC Augustus and Paullus' friends rebuilt it in the name of Aemilius; Pliny counted it among the three most beautiful buildings in the world, and M. Lepidus restored it again in AD 22.
